details.body: In `water_change.rs` lines 67 and 85, `bicarbonate_mg_total` is independently retained and added from the source profile before `resolve_carbonate_state` overwrites it at line 95. The state contract (`docs/carbonate_state_contract.md`) says 'bicarbonate_mg_total should never again be incremented independently by chemistry logic once the new solver lands.' Remove the independent mutations of `bicarbonate_mg_total` in `apply_water_change` (lines 67 and 85) since the resolve at line 95 computes the correct value from DIC and alkalinity. This also applies to `rescale_totals_for_volume` (water.rs:204) which rescales `bicarbonate_mg_total` — since it's a cached projection, it should be re-derived via resolve rather than linearly scaled (though in the rescale case the result happens to be numerically identical).

The negligible-alkalinity fallback (chemistry.rs lines 82-88) returns pH 7.0 with all DIC reported as CO2(aq). This is per the contract spec but creates a gameplay-critical blind spot: when nitrification depletes alkalinity to zero (nitrogen_cycle.rs line 349-350 clamps to 0.0) while respiration continues adding DIC, the solver reports pH 7.0 instead of the acidic pH (roughly 5.0-5.5) that represents an acid crash — the single most dangerous event in aquarium keeping. Consider returning a low pH estimate (e.g., from the Henderson-Hasselbalch approximation treating all DIC as CO2, giving pH ≈ pKa1 - log10(DIC/Alk_trace)) or at minimum emitting a structured warning event when this fallback fires with nonzero DIC, so the gameplay layer can surface the acid crash to the player.

The pre-existing `hatch_produces_juveniles` test in shrimp_population.rs is failing (adults drop from 10 to 2 over 60 days with condition_index=0.652 and zero juveniles produced). This failure predates the 6e5.4.2 changes (confirmed at commit 99c61dc) and is not introduced by the carbonate solver work. However, `cargo test` currently fails due to this test. Either fix the underlying shrimp population dynamics issue or update the test expectations to match the current behavior before merging.

Fix the post-solve pH clamping split. `resolve_carbonate_state()` writes the raw equilibrium result into `water.ph` (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:162-170`), but `enforce_invariants()` later clamps only `water.ph` to `5.5..=8.5` (`crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:89-95`). `TankSnapshot::from_state()` then recomputes `co2_aq_mmol_per_l` from the unclamped carbonate inputs while using the clamped `water.ph` for NH3 (`crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:76-88`), and save loading re-solves back to the unclamped value (`crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:309-330`). Any state whose solver pH falls outside `5.5..=8.5` ends up with mutually inconsistent pH/CO2/bicarbonate behavior and non-idempotent save-loads. Clamp at the carbonate-solver boundary or reproject all derived carbonate fields together after clamping.

Recalibrate or reject the shipped source-water carbonate presets under the new solver. Startup water materialization now derives pH from `dic_mg_c_per_l` and `alkalinity_meq_per_l` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:87-110`), but the existing presets still encode ratios from the old shortcut: `soft_acidic.toml` uses `12.0` mg C/L with `1.07` meq/L (`crates/tank_data/data/source_water/soft_acidic.toml:8-16`), `moderate.toml` uses `15.0` with `1.249` (`crates/tank_data/data/source_water/moderate.toml:8-16`), and `hard_shrimp.toml` uses `21.0` with `1.785` (`crates/tank_data/data/source_water/hard_shrimp.toml:8-16`). Plugging those values into the implemented `solve_carbonate_equilibrium()` yields roughly pH `9.12`, `8.29`, and `8.68`, so the `soft_acidic` preset is not acidic at all and two shipped presets immediately hit the invariant ceiling. `SourceWaterPreset::validate()` (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:34-70`) does not catch this. Update the preset DIC/alk pairs or add a derived-pH validation gate before shipping.

The fallback_all_co2 path (chemistry.rs:85-92) reports all DIC as CO2 with zero HCO3-/CO3--, yet the pH is computed from acid_only_fallback_ph which implies nonzero HCO3-. At the clamped pH of 5.5, HCO3- should be ~12% of CO2 (10^(5.5-6.35) ≈ 0.14). The species output is thermodynamically inconsistent with the reported pH. This causes bicarbonate_mg_total to be artificially zeroed in low-alkalinity water, slightly distorting TDS/conductivity for those regimes. Fix: call carbonate_species_for_ph at the solved (clamped) pH instead of hardcoding all DIC as CO2, or document why the inconsistency is acceptable.

The design contract (docs/carbonate_state_contract.md line 112) specifies that fallback paths should 'emit a structured diagnostic' when triggered. The implementation in fallback_all_co2, fallback_high_buffer, and fallback_outside_quadratic_envelope (chemistry.rs:85-118) silently returns results without any logging or tracing. Add at minimum a tracing::debug! or equivalent so operators can detect when the solver hits edge cases during gameplay.

No integration test verifies that the shipped source water profiles (hard_shrimp, moderate, soft_acidic, ro_like) produce meaningfully differentiated initial pH values from the new solver. Add a test that constructs WaterState from each profile and asserts ordering (e.g., hard_shrimp pH > moderate pH > soft_acidic pH) and minimum spread (e.g., at least 0.3 pH units between hardest and softest).

The v2→v3 migration (save.rs:283-314) rescales bicarbonate_mg_total along with all dissolved fields, but normalize_loaded_carbonate_state (save.rs:339-348) unconditionally overwrites it after all migrations complete. The migration rescale of bicarbonate_mg_total is dead work. Consider removing it from the dissolved_fields list with a comment explaining that bicarbonate is now solver-derived, to avoid misleading future migration authors into thinking bicarbonate rescaling is load-bearing.

Fix the exact-zero DIC discontinuity in the carbonate solver. `crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:145-147` returns `NEUTRAL_FALLBACK` whenever DIC reaches zero, but the same solver returns `pH = 8.5` for arbitrarily small positive DIC under the same alkalinity. Because live update paths clamp DIC to exactly zero before resolving (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:304-313`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/plant_growth.rs:147-149`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/algae_growth.rs:112-115`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/algae_growth.rs:193-196`), a strongly photosynthetic tank can jump from the alkaline ceiling to neutral in one tick. The zero-DIC branch should use a limit-consistent fallback instead of snapping to `pH 7.0`.

Unify source-water carbonate validation and runtime resolution onto one authoritative contract. `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:44-46` and `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:150-169` reject zero-alkalinity / nonzero-DIC source waters via a separate `predicted_carbonate_ph` implementation, while runtime source-water validation in `crates/tank_core/src/types/source_water.rs:31-65` accepts the same chemistry and materialization resolves it through `crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:87-110` and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:74-79` / `crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:152-156`. Right now the same source-water payload can be rejected when loaded from TOML but accepted when it arrives via a save or runtime catalog, which means preset loading and simulation no longer share one carbonate contract. Move both paths to the same helper/validation rule.

In carbonate_species_for_ph (chemistry.rs:66-73), the function receives dic_mol_per_l but after pH clamping at line 290, species are reprojected at the clamped pH. While species fractions still sum to DIC (mass conservation is preserved), the implicit alkalinity (HCO3 + 2*CO3) at the clamped pH no longer equals the input alkalinity. This is a deliberate design trade-off and is currently undocumented at the call site. Add a brief comment at line 290-292 noting that DIC conservation is maintained but alkalinity consistency is sacrificed at the clamp boundaries, so future maintainers don't try to 'fix' this by rebalancing.

The bicarbonate_mg_total field in WaterState is a solver-derived cache (set by resolve_carbonate_state) but is included in total_tracked_ions_mg() (water.rs:215) which feeds TDS and conductivity calculations. Between a mutation of DIC/alkalinity and the next resolve_carbonate_state call, bicarbonate_mg_total is stale. The nitrogen cycle (nitrogen_cycle.rs:348-350) modifies alkalinity without resolving, relying on the subsequent chemistry step. This stale-window is safe today because the engine step ordering guarantees resolution before any TDS read, but it's a footgun for future system additions. Consider adding a doc comment on total_tracked_ions_mg() noting that callers must ensure resolve_carbonate_state has been called after the most recent DIC/alkalinity mutation.

Correctness: `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:331-340` seeds missing `animal.reserve_g` from existing shrimp biomass during the v3->v4 migration. That changes the physical state of every migrated save instead of preserving it. `reserve_g` is documented as post-feeding retained reserve, not structural shrimp biomass (`crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:94-99`), and it is counted as separate N/C mass in the budget (`crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:246-248`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:331-333`) and later spent for hatching/maturation (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:641-651`) or exported on shrimp removal (`crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:402-408`). A schema-3 save with existing shrimp therefore gains free reserve, extra total mass, and potentially immediate reproduction/maturation progress just by loading. The migration should preserve old behavior by leaving `reserve_g` at its serde default of `0.0`, or by introducing a separate non-budgeted compatibility/display field if an inspectable value is still desired.

In `TankSnapshot::from_state` (snapshot.rs:76-87), the snapshot reads `ph` from the cached `state.water.ph` (line 87) but reads `co2_aq_mmol_per_l` from a freshly re-solved `solve_carbonate_equilibrium` call (lines 76-81). If the state is ever produced on stale inputs (DIC/Alk mutated without a resolve call), the pH and CO2 in the snapshot would be mutually inconsistent. Since the solver is deterministic and all current paths maintain consistency this is safe today, but using `carbonate_eq.ph` instead of `state.water.ph` for the snapshot's `ph` field would make the snapshot self-consistent by construction and eliminate the coupling to the resolve-before-snapshot precondition.

The `bicarbonate_mg_per_l` field in `SourceWaterProfile` (source_water.rs:25) is set during `WaterState::from_source_profile_for_volume_l` (water.rs:105) but immediately overwritten by `resolve_carbonate_state` (water.rs:110). During water changes, only DIC and alkalinity from the source profile are mixed in — `bicarbonate_mg_per_l` is not used. The field is effectively dead input for chemistry but is still validated and carried through presets. Add a code comment on the field documenting that it is display/documentation only and not an authoritative chemistry input, to prevent future developers from tuning it expecting it to affect equilibrium behavior.

Do not seed `animal.reserve_g` from live shrimp counts in `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:333-369`. `reserve_g` is a separate stored material pool, not the structural biomass already represented by `adults_count`/`juveniles_count`: it is counted independently in the elemental budgets (`crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:246-248`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:332-333`) and can be spent to create new shrimp biomass (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:639-657`). Reconstructing it from existing shrimp counts injects extra N/C into every migrated v3 save and can immediately fund hatching/maturation that the saved state never actually contained.

Rework the new detritus-appetite cap in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:148-165` to use one consistent mass basis. `food_demand`/`periph_consumed` are raw periphyton biomass grams, but `detritus_consumed` and `daily_food_consumed_g` are organic-matter routing grams (`crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:86-89`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:379-385`). Because the remainder is computed as `food_demand - periph_consumed`, detritus-heavy diets can still overshoot the intended daily intake cap by roughly 4x at the default N:C ratio, and the added regression test at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:835-871` currently encodes the same mixed-unit expectation.
